D01.observed: Direct labels and a matched trained-token output were tested. The Qwen browser path passed a two-message smoke. A separate two-output BERT export preserved all 100 decisions in actual browser execution. A shared two/four-layer browser model also matches every saved exit; typed input loads only its 44.5 MB adaptive graphs. Two original vocabulary rows matched constrained one-token decisions on 50 reused messages with 6.6% less whole-path time.
D01.remaining: Returning an enum alone showed no reliable timing gain; the newer paths also differ in cache construction and generation overhead. No general output-format superiority.

D02.observed: Fixed early, middle, late and full-depth classifiers were actually timed. Follow-up heads at 22/23/24 skip exactly the recorded blocks; the late shortcuts introduced new toxic misses.
D02.remaining: No general layer at which arbitrary answers become ready.

D03.observed: Actual input-dependent exits execute in Python and the browser. On 500 unused messages, the original shared BERT rule proposes 400 layer-2 exits and preserves all full-depth decisions, projecting 40% fewer blocks. Its model gets 440/500 correct. The selected distilled model gets 451/500 but increases toxic misses from 3 to 5; its learned risk check stops fewer cases than the confidence rule. Actual execution on the first 50 fresh messages preserved decisions and reduced time by 34.7%.
D03.remaining: The fresh remainder had only 18 toxic messages. This preserves the reference model's errors and does not establish rare-error reliability or arbitrary-rule handling. Earlier Qwen reliability gates failed.

D04.observed: Changing-rule and unfamiliar-input tests expose failures.
D04.remaining: No demonstrated arbitrary instruction following or long-conversation robustness.

D05.observed: Actual layer traces and request times measured. Fixed-prefix reuse and four-message batches preserved all 100 predictions while reducing own paired workload times by 37.9% and 9.7%; every message still uses all 24 layers. Combined prefix reuse plus batches of four reduced its paired 50-message workload by 42.9%, preserving all decisions; all 24 layers execute. Original shared BERT saved 34.7% in three actual CPU passes on the first 50 fresh messages, preserving predictions and layer traces; a separate consumed 50 browser test saved 36.4% with real shared-state continuation. Loading is excluded and separately reported.
D05.remaining: These are warm CPU workload measurements, not live-response latency, independent-hardware replication or accepted moderation quality.

D06.observed: Original cascade and conservative follow-up tested on 100 unused messages. Strict version preserved decisions but avoided Qwen only twice and saved less than 1% time.
D06.remaining: No useful quality-preserving speed improvement established by the conservative follow-up; broader datasets and error-budget validation remain.

C02.observed: Earlier ScreenSpot region selection found 25/30 present targets. On a fresh OSWorld-G stress test, it found 8/25 present targets. A frozen confidence cutoff withheld all 25 author-labelled infeasible requests, but allowed only 4 present requests: 2 correct and 2 wrong. Predicted-point cropping improved 2/10 to 3/10 with another complete model pass.
C02.remaining: Useful click coverage and reliable accepted actions remain unresolved. A cutoff returns uncertainty, not learned absent-target recognition; infeasible requests can include impossible actions on present controls.

C03.observed: Coordinate model still runs all 28 transformer blocks.
C03.remaining: Needs trained intermediate pointer heads and reliable grounding/abstention controls.

L01.observed: The full 262,144-token window opens on two cards with a 16-bit cache. Read speed falls from 3,280 tokens a second at 8K to 1,550 at 250K and write speed from 127 to 26. Drafting gave exactly the no-drafting answer at every length. Of 720 buried codes, every one was right at 60K; from 120K to 250K about 1 look-up in 40 returned a look-alike neighbour. No value was invented and no region of the context was lost.
L01.remaining: Single-server first looks on one machine, not package numbers. The window that opens is larger than the window that is look-up exact (about 60K in the hardest test).

L02.observed: An exact prefix cache that keeps only state made while reading gave the uncached answer in 99 of 99 cases with drafting on, including second and third turns. A question over a cached 200K context starts in 2.0 s instead of 114 s; an edit in the middle of a 30K prompt resumes from the last kept state. A cold read is 14-27% slower.
L02.remaining: One user; token ids compared, not scores; prompts above 30K tested only by a cold repeat at 120K; the one-card server untested.

L03.status: Measured pilot, one seed; longer runs in progress
L03.observed: On a 121,000-token stream of counter updates, keeping everything in the window got 24 of 24 in 26 minutes; summarising at 75% of a 32K budget got 24 of 24 in 41 minutes; the paper’s self-editing agent got 19 of 24 in 64 minutes. All five losses were batches its own rollback-and-retry removed after delivery; the model’s own edits lost nothing.
L03.remaining: One task family and one seed. An improved agent and a stream larger than the window (480K) are running. Removed text is gone unless it is saved somewhere.

L04.status: Measured pilot, one seed; longer run in progress
L04.observed: With files allowed, the model kept its data on disk and got 24 of 24 in 1.9 minutes, holding at most 8.2K (self-editing) and 8.9K (no management) tokens of context: 14 to 22 times faster than keeping everything or summarising.
L04.remaining: One task family and one seed; the 480K stream with files allowed is running. Works when code or search does the reading; text the model must itself understand still has to pass through the card.

L05.observed: On 5.0M tokens of real agent sessions, strict no-loss cleaning freed 1.8% and moving large tool outputs to disk 7.5% (about one in three was read back later). Re-sent earlier thinking is about 10% of a typical call and up to 56%. A 32K window holds about 33K tokens’ worth after no-loss cleaning.
L05.remaining: Blanket dropping of earlier thinking left one run stuck for 2.6 hours with no answer; it is safe only when the working state lives elsewhere.

L06.observed: The cache is exactly 64 KiB per token, about 13 GB for 200K tokens. With a 12.7 GB/s drive (measured) and 9-16 GB/s uploads to the card, streaming it on every written token would give roughly 3-4 tokens a second against about 35 in video memory.
L06.remaining: Nothing built. Parking and restoring a whole conversation’s cache is designed, not built or measured.
